text:
Sasha: quick heads-up — running `terraform plan` against staging and it gets stuck on computing diff for a k8s manifest, then flakes with a remote state lock. anyone seen this pattern before?

Ben: saw similar when an external controller mutates annotations right after import. can you paste the exact error?

Sasha: here’s the relevant tail of the plan output:
```
Refreshing state...
Error: Error refreshing state: remote state locked (ID: apply-2026-03-15)

Refreshing provider plugin...
kubernetes_manifest.myapp_config: Refreshing state...
kubernetes_manifest.myapp_config: Resource has drifted: metadata.annotations."last-applied" changed outside of Terraform
Plan: 0 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy.
Computing diffs... hangs
```

Rajesh: that "last-applied" thing is usually the kubectl/apply annotation or a controller (argocd/flux) re-writing. If the annotation timestamp flips each reconcile, plan will constantly see changes.

Emily: can you run `terraform state show kubernetes_manifest.myapp_config` and also `kubectl get manifest -o yaml` to confirm who is changing it?

Sasha: ran them — state shows annotation value A, actual cluster shows value B with a timestamp. argocd is reconciling every 30s.

Ben: two quick options: (1) add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations] }` to the resource so plan stops chasing the annotation, or (2) import the exact cluster object into TF so timestamps match. But import + controller still means you’ll get churn unless you ignore annotations.

Rajesh: also note the remote state lock error — looks like CI started an apply concurrently. infra-oncall-bot?

infra-oncall-bot: detected concurrent apply. Lock created by run: ci/infra-staging/2026-03-15T09:04:22Z. TTL 10m.

Sasha: ah yeah, a PR pipeline retriggered while I was testing.

Emily: for immediate unblock: 1) cancel the running CI apply, or 2) use `terraform plan -lock=false` (only if you are sure no other apply is happening). Otherwise increasing `-lock-timeout=5m` may help but it won’t fix churn from argocd.

Sasha: trying `-lock=false` locally to see plan diff while I debug argocd.

Ben: long-term: either teach argocd to ignore that specific annotation (recommended), or move manifest ownership fully to Terraform (and disable that part in argocd).

Rajesh: if you go with ignore_changes, prefer a targeted map key like `metadata[0].annotations["last-applied"]` if provider supports it, so you don’t ignore other useful annotation changes.

Sasha: got a plan now (with -lock=false) that shows only annotation changes. I’ll push a small TF patch to add ignore_changes and open a follow-up PR to update argocd config.

deploy-bot: CI: cancel request received for run ci/infra-staging/2026-03-15T09:04:22Z by Sasha.

Emily: ping me on the PR for the argocd tweak, happy to review. Also let's add a short note in infra runbook about this common pattern (k8s annotation churn).

Sasha: thanks — will do. cc @Rajesh for review on the targeted ignore_changes. :thumbsup:

Ben: nice and tidy. TL;DR for slack search: annotation churn from controller + concurrent apply lock => plan stalls; fix by targeted ignore_changes or transferring ownership and avoid concurrent CI applies.
